title: Added Sugars: Hidden Sources and Their Effects on Health

authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: Where do added sugars hide in everyday foods, and how do they affect health?
reader_intent: Identify hidden added sugars in packaged foods and understand their health effects.
desired_reader_outcome: Reader knows AHA's added-sugar limits, the many names for sugar, common hidden-sugar foods, and practical reduction strategies.

claims.proposition: The average American consumes approximately 17 teaspoons (71g) of added sugar per day.
claims.recommended_action: A commonly cited NHANES-derived figure; not independently reverified against a primary CDC/NHANES source this session.

claims.proposition: AHA recommends limiting added sugar to 6 tsp (25g) for women and 9 tsp (36g) for men.
claims.recommended_action: Matches the newly added claim-aha-added-sugar-limit almost exactly (that claim's primary source states the recommendation in calories — 100/150 kcal/day — and the gram figures are the standard conversion).

internal_link_recommendations.reason: Near-duplicate reader job with more label-specific detail.

disposition_reason: This reader job (hidden sugar sources, many names for sugar, health effects) is heavily duplicated by understanding-food-labels-added-sugars, which additionally covers the FDA's 2020 label-format change and the Dietary Guidelines' separate <10%-of-calories figure with more regulatory context. This article's distinct value — its longer, more example-rich 'where sugar hides' food list — is worth preserving in the merge.
required_research: Verify the ~17 tsp/71g average daily added-sugar consumption figure against a primary CDC/NHANES source.
recommended_rewrite_scope: Fold this article's more extensive hidden-sugar food examples into the survivor during rewrite.
